title: MLB: overview
d: The MLB is American's baseball competition, founded 1903 with 30 teams.
definition: The MLB is American's baseball competition, founded 1903 with 30 teams.
description: The MLB is the American baseball competition, founded 1903, featuring 30 teams. It is played in 162-game season; 3 playoff rounds to the World Series format. The Yankees' 27 World Series titles lead. Leagues are the weekly heartbeat of their sport — where rivalries live, stars are made, and communities gather. This database covers the league's history, format, clubs, champions, records, and how to follow it.

title: History and origins
d: MLB was founded in 1903. The Yankees' 27 World Series titles lead..
definition: MLB was founded in 1903. The Yankees' 27 World Series titles lead..
description: The MLB began in 1903. The Yankees' 27 World Series titles lead. Like every great league, it started small — a few clubs, a simple idea — and grew as the sport grew. Its history is written in dynasties and droughts, in rule changes forced by controversy, and in the generations of fans who inherited their club from their parents.

title: Competition format
d: MLB format: 162-game season; 3 playoff rounds to the World Series.
definition: MLB format: 162-game season; 3 playoff rounds to the World Series.
description: The MLB plays a 162-game season; 3 playoff rounds to the World Series. Format decides everything about a season: how many games matter, when to peak, whether consistency or knockout nerve wins. Learn the format and you understand every tactical decision — why teams rest stars, why some games are played for draws, and why the final weeks turn chaotic.

title: Season structure
d: A MLB season runs through regular play into playoffs or a run-in.
definition: A MLB season runs through regular play into playoffs or a run-in.
description: A MLB season has phases: the early feeling-out, the midseason grind, and the run-in where every point is precious. Fixture congestion, travel, and injuries reshape the table; squad depth wins long seasons while momentum wins short ones. The teams that manage all three phases lift trophies.

title: The championship
d: Winning the MLB means surviving the full season and delivering when it counts.
definition: Winning the MLB means surviving the full season and delivering when it counts.
description: The MLB championship is decided by 162-game season; 3 playoff rounds to the World Series. Champions share traits: consistency against weaker opposition, nerve in the big games, and luck with injuries. Dynasties form when great recruitment meets great coaching; droughts end when a generation matures together. The trophy is lifted in a moment but won over months.

title: League records
d: The MLB record book: titles, points, and scoring marks.
definition: The MLB record book: titles, points, and scoring marks.
description: The MLB record book holds the numbers every fan argues about: most titles, highest points totals, scoring records, longest unbeaten runs. The Yankees' 27 World Series titles lead. Records give seasons their stakes — the chase for a record can matter as much as the title race, and the record-holders become the league's immortals.

title: Great rivalries
d: The MLB's fiercest rivalries define its calendar.
definition: The MLB's fiercest rivalries define its calendar.
description: Rivalries are the MLB's lifeblood: derbies split cities and families, and rivalry weeks produce the season's most intense atmospheres. These games are rarely about form — history, pride, and bragging rights outweigh tactics. Win the derby and the season is forgiven; lose it and nothing else quite matters.

title: Star players
d: The MLB's stars carry the league's global profile.
definition: The MLB's stars carry the league's global profile.
description: Star players make the MLB appointment viewing: the scorers, the playmakers, the personalities. Leagues market their stars, and stars repay it with moments that travel worldwide. But the league's soul is also the unsung starters — the defenders and workers who make the stars shine.

title: Money and business
d: The MLB runs on broadcast rights, sponsorship, and matchday revenue.
definition: The MLB runs on broadcast rights, sponsorship, and matchday revenue.
description: The business of the MLB: broadcast deals fund the prize money, sponsors fund the clubs, and matchday revenue funds the atmosphere. Financial fair play and salary caps — where they exist — try to keep competition honest. Money does not guarantee titles, but its absence guarantees struggle.

title: The fans
d: MLB fans: the songs, the scarves, and the away days.
definition: MLB fans: the songs, the scarves, and the away days.
description: The fans make the MLB: the songs that never stop, the tifos, the away-day pilgrimages. Fan culture differs by club and country but shares one truth — the league belongs to the people in the stands as much as the people on the field. Respect the culture: learn the songs, honor the traditions, protect the atmosphere.

title: Path to the pros
d: Reaching the MLB runs through academies, colleges, or lower leagues.
definition: Reaching the MLB runs through academies, colleges, or lower leagues.
description: The path to the MLB runs through youth academies, school and college programs, and lower professional leagues. Scouts watch for athleticism, game intelligence, and character; the final step is always mentality. For every star, a thousand talented players fell short — the difference is usually professionalism, not talent.

title: How to follow
d: Follow the MLB: broadcasts, schedules, and storylines to watch.
definition: Follow the MLB: broadcasts, schedules, and storylines to watch.
description: Following the MLB: learn the schedule rhythm, pick a club (or let one pick you), and follow the storylines — the title race, the relegation battle, the breakout star. Watch with the sound up for the songs and down for the analysis sometimes. The league rewards the regular viewer: context compounds week after week.

title: The future
d: The MLB's future: expansion, technology, and the next generation.
definition: The MLB's future: expansion, technology, and the next generation.
description: The future of the MLB: expansion to new markets, video officiating, data-driven tactics, and the constant negotiation between tradition and growth. Leagues that honor their history while embracing change thrive; those that freeze in time fade. The next decade will look different — the songs will stay the same.

title: Dynasties
d: The MLB's dynasties set the standard every era chases.
definition: The MLB's dynasties set the standard every era chases.
description: Every MLB era has its dynasty: the club that figured it out first and kept figuring it out. Dynasties are built on recruitment, coaching stability, and a core that peaks together — and they end when the core ages or the genius leaves. Studying dynasties teaches what sustained excellence actually costs.

title: The relegation battle
d: At the bottom of the MLB, survival is its own trophy.
definition: At the bottom of the MLB, survival is its own trophy.
description: Where the MLB has relegation, the bottom of the table is its own competition: survival worth hundreds of millions, played with desperation. Relegation battles produce the season's rawest drama — final-day escapes and collapses that fans never forget. The drop changes clubs for years; avoiding it is a triumph.

title: Transfer market
d: The MLB transfer market: how squads are built and broken.
definition: The MLB transfer market: how squads are built and broken.
description: The MLB transfer market is the league's second season: rumors, medicals, and deadline-day chaos. Smart clubs buy for the system and sell at the peak; desperate clubs overpay in January. The window's winners are often decided years later, when the prospect becomes the star — or the flop.

title: Tactical trends
d: How MLB tactics evolve: the ideas winning right now.
definition: How MLB tactics evolve: the ideas winning right now.
description: Tactical trends in the MLB move in cycles: the high press gives way to the low block, possession yields to transition. Coaches copy what wins until someone solves it, then the wheel turns. The league's current meta — its fashionable formation and pressing scheme — is always a response to whoever dominated last.

title: Iconic matches
d: Matches that define the MLB: the ones fans still talk about.
definition: Matches that define the MLB: the ones fans still talk about.
description: Every MLB has matches that became folklore: the comeback, the title decider, the upset that broke the script. These games are replayed for decades because they compressed everything the league is into ninety minutes. Ask any fan for their iconic match and you will learn what their club means to them.

title: Manager greats
d: The MLB's legendary managers shaped eras.
definition: The MLB's legendary managers shaped eras.
description: The MLB's great managers are its philosophers and its lightning rods: builders of dynasties, masters of the press conference, tacticians who changed the meta. Players come and go, but a great manager's system can define a club for a decade. The touchline is the league's theater within the theater.

title: Stadium guide
d: The MLB's great grounds: cathedrals of the sport.
definition: The MLB's great grounds: cathedrals of the sport.
description: The grounds of the MLB range from century-old cathedrals to futuristic arenas. Each has its character: the steep stand that roars, the away end tucked in the corner, the pre-match rituals outside. Visiting them all is the fan's pilgrimage — the league is best understood from the stands, not the sofa.

title: Broadcast guide
d: Watching the MLB: broadcasts, pundits, and the second screen.
definition: Watching the MLB: broadcasts, pundits, and the second screen.
description: Watching the MLB well means knowing the rhythms: the early game, the main event, the highlights show. Find pundits who teach rather than shout, follow reliable journalists for the inside story, and use the second screen for stats — not arguments. The broadcast is the global stadium; learn its language.

title: Women's game
d: The women's MLB: the fastest-growing part of the sport.
definition: The women's MLB: the fastest-growing part of the sport.
description: The women's game connected to the MLB is the sport's fastest-growing frontier: rising crowds, rising standards, rising investment. Its history was suppressed in many places for decades; its present is a correction running at full speed. Follow it with the same seriousness — the football, and the stories, deserve it.
